rubric_items.reason: All 12 acceptance criteria (S-1 AC1-5, S-2 AC1-2, S-3 AC1-5) have at least one test. Two mappings are loose: TP-15 claims S-3/AC3 and TP-16 claims S-3/AC5, but neither proves that criterion.

Page rendering and links are tested at unit level with jsdom. Counting, paging, sort, filters and search are tested at integration level against the database. No end-to-end tests. Each check uses the cheapest level that proves it.

There is a negative test for the new with_today flag (TP-15), a next-day boundary test (TP-3) and a zero-count edge test (TP-6/TP-7). Missing: a test at the IST/UTC midnight edge, and negative tests for any link-target filters this change adds.

Tools match the strategy (Vitest, Supertest, PostgreSQL 16, fixed clock, jsdom, Testing Library), and the plan follows the no-e2e gap and the requirement-ID naming rule. It does not name the test files or folders the tests go in.
Titles are short and concrete, and the frontmatter and body agree. Tests are mapped to stories and criteria but not to REQ ids, although the plan requires names to start with REQ ids.
